title: Andy Taylor Was Full of Surprises: Six Deep-Dive Career Moments
summary: Following his death at the age of 65, Billboard has highlighted some impressive, but overlooked moments from Andy Taylor’s Hall of Fame career.
contentText:
Andy Taylor , the founding guitarist with Duran Duran , who passed away Monday (Nov. 23) following a years-long battle with prostate cancer, aged 65 , just might be the most underrated musician to emerge from the early 1980s.

Taylor, who would also form The Power Station, enjoyed a solo career and was something of a serial collaborator, stood tall in a golden era for electric guitarists. Even the slickest commercial pop songs had destructive guitar solos, the type of which seem to be lost to this generation and last.

Forget the Cold War, there was another arms race where the weapons of choice were plugged-in six-strings, with rows of effects pedals. Eddie Van Halen, Steve Vai, Joe Satriani, The Edge, Steve Stevens, Yngwie Malmsteen, Steve Lukather. It was an expansive group, and Andy Taylor was a member in good standing.

Born in Tynemouth and raised in Cullercoats, Northumberland, in north east England, Taylor was the wild boy in Duran Duran – his autobiography from 2008 even carried that title.

Here was a roguish rockstar with fast hands, itchy feet, who didn’t follow trends, but had many, many followers. But because of his breakthrough with Duran Duran, a band that drew a mystifying flood of hate from critics of the time, Taylor’s talents were largely overlooked.

What he did next, couldn’t be ignored.

Duran Duran split into two camps following the release of the 1985 James Bond hit “A View to a Kill.” Andy and John Taylor formed The Power Station, the funk-rock supergroup with Robert Palmer at the front, and Tony Thompson at the back, while Simon Le Bon, Nick Rhodes and Roger Taylor launched Arcadia, a collaborative-stacked project that, in an alternative universe, would’ve been Duran Duran’s fourth studio album.

With The Power Station, Andy Taylor was unleashed. We got shredding, finger tapping, the works. Taylor contributed to the Duran Duran album from 1986, Notorious , then he was out. Fifteen years later, he returned to the band with original drummer Roger Taylor, to reunite the Fab Five. He contributed to the 2004 album Astronaut , and again on the 2023 collection Danse Macabre .

The music world learned of his illness when, in 2022 , Duran Duran was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. Taylor, his bandmates explained, as they read out a letter from the guitarist, was unable to attend due to illness.

Billboard has compiled six deep-dive moments from Andy Taylor’s Hall of Fame career.
